name: c3-public-go-api
description: Go port of c3-public-api (public API: analytics passthrough, Bearer-gated mail bridge with the delivery ledger, SuperApp config artifact, Profile > Connect with mailed one-time codes), shadow stage: runs next to the Node container on its own port, outside every request path (ticket #1882).

native_build._doc: Same multi-stage template as c3bot-relay-go (#1873): compiled in golang on the arch-matched runner (oci-apps is arm64), shipped as one static binary on distroless static nonroot.

mail._doc: JSON-in -> SMTP-out: replicates the aa-sui_tools-http-to-smtp-proxy-api Rust binary contract so the CF Worker does not need any change. Delivery to Maddy:25 (MX-style, plain SMTP over WG); Maddy's dual-write relays every local delivery to Stalwart:2025, so no shadow leg here (2026-08-18: shadow removed — it duplicated every message).
mail._doc_targets: #1811 parallel fan-out. The CF Worker picks one target per request with the X-Mail-Target header and calls this bridge once per store, in parallel: maddy-direct (maddy stores only, no Stalwart mirror) and stalwart (Stalwart SMTP ingest :2025). No header = maddy = the primary above (maddy:25, which still mirrors to Stalwart), so an older Worker keeps working unchanged. Never send one message to both maddy (mirroring) and stalwart: that duplicates it in Stalwart.

profile_connect._doc: Superapp Configs>Profile>Connect (#566). POST /profile/connect/start mails a one-time code to mail_to over the same maddy:25 delivery as /mail/http-to-smtp; POST /profile/connect/fetch {code} returns {schema, bundle} read AS IS from the read-only bind mount of cloud-vault E0_configs/<bundle_file>. Bearer (Caddy mkProtected + in-app X-Auth-User check) AND the mailed code are both required. #589: the bundle is plaintext in the vault (private repo); no age key, no sops on this VM — a sops-encrypted file on the mount is refused (bundle_unreadable), because it is exactly the file the phone cannot read (#585).
profile_connect._doc_bundle: The bundle dir on oci-analytics is deploy.host_sync.profile_bundle.host_dir (cloud-vault Shared/configs/: was configs/, then E0_configs/ until vault 6c0aab8 renamed the sections; cloud-infra host-sync-declaration.test.sh #7 checks every vault_dir/file against the vault checkout, so the next rename goes red in CI instead of on the ship): the ONE declaration compose.nix mounts read-only at bundle_mount and the engine fills. bundle_file and schema_file name the files inside that mount; test-profile-connect.ts F5 pins that host_sync ships exactly them.

limits._doc_request_timeout_ms: Caps nodemailer connectionTimeout + greetingTimeout + socketTimeout for the Maddy:25 delivery (warm completes <3s). 15000ms headroom retained from the removed Stalwart shadow leg (2026-08-18: shadow removed — Maddy's dual-write already relays every delivery to Stalwart:2025).
limits._doc_smtp_timeout_ms: #1819: the SMTP session's own connection/greeting/socket timeouts, decoupled from the HTTP answer (request_timeout_ms). oci-mail under swap and CPU steal accepted messages after the 15 s answer deadline; the old shared timeout aborted the session, answered 500, and each Worker retry opened a new session, storing the mail 2-3 times. Now the session keeps running up to this long, the answer is 504 pending, and a retry joins it (shared/delivery-ledger.ts).
limits._doc_dedupe_ttl_ms: #1819: how long a delivered (target, Message-ID, rcpt) is remembered, so a late Worker retry is answered delivered without a second send. 30 min covers the Worker's inline try plus its background retries many times over.

parity-compare._doc: Reference = the Node service (api/index.ts under tsx, npm ci in CI); the Go port; each with its own fake analytics backends and fake SMTP store; the same ordered request list (health/ready/HEAD, Fastify 404 shapes, CORS, rate limit with the exhausted-client allow-list, analytics passthrough incl. body parsing, the mail bridge: auth gate, body shapes, targets, dedupe, failure, pending/join, Profile > Connect code flow, SuperApp config) must give identical status, headers and raw bodies, and the fakes must have seen identical backend requests and SMTP messages.

parity-mutation.cmd: o=$(mktemp); PARITY_MUTATE=1 PARITY_REQUIRE=1 go test -count=1 -timeout 9m -tags parity -run TestParity ./parity/ >"$o" 2>&1; grep -q 'requests differ' "$o"
parity-mutation._doc: Mutation proof: the Go port's rate limit is one lower; the harness must report differing requests.

_doc_shadow: Shadow stage (#1882). The live Node c3-public-api (container c3-public-api, oci-apps 10.0.0.6:8087) is untouched. No env_file (the vault mapping of OPENOBSERVE_AUTHORIZATION for this service name belongs to the switch-over: the openobserve passthrough carries the caller's Authorization until then) and no baked SuperApp artifact (the Node image gets build-cloud-superapp-<user>.json through a CI-resolved symlink; the Go image needs the service-shipped Dockerfile flavour for that, a switch-over prerequisite): /superapp/config answers 404 for every user until then, as the Node service does for an absent artifact. The profile bundle is mounted read-only from the same host dir the Node service uses. Binds the oci-apps WG IP on port 8097.
